title: P0 Safety contract (core/pkg/safety): ownership rollback, TRIAL, kill switch, Reset
description:
Parent: cross-os-ymh



## Background

P0 contract (COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN.md Section 3.10, Section 8). Safety model: ownership rollback, IntegrationState (NOT a system snapshot), TRIAL trial-state, explicit-approve permissions (no auto-approve, not even safe defaults), kill switch (PANIC STOP), Reset Everything.



## Reasoning

CrossOS intercepts input system-wide. A bad rule or plugin must be reversible in one click and never strand OS state. The rollback boundary must be explicit now: CrossOS rolls back CrossOS-owned state only, never arbitrary OS state (Accessibility grants, foreign login items).



## Scope

- IntegrationState + IntegrationRecord types (plugin ID, type, identifier, state-before, rollback func)

- Ownership tracking on every system modification (creator plugin ID, timestamp, rollback procedure)

- TRIAL transactional enable: DISABLED to TRIAL to ENABLED; crash/timeout/kill-switch during TRIAL to DISABLED; 30s safe-mode confirm/rollback

- Kill switch: disable interception + plugin actions + flush/close (login item stays)

- Reset Everything: remove login item, disable extension, clean CrossOS-owned state, verify no process remains

- Explicit-approve permission prompts with least-privilege manifest check (over-scoped manifests rejected)



## Pass criteria

- [ ] Safety package with IntegrationState, ownership records, TRIAL flow, kill switch, reset

- [ ] No auto-approve path anywhere (test: enabling without user confirm stays un-enabled)

- [ ] Rollback removes/restores only CrossOS-owned resources (documented boundary)



## Plan refs

COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN.md: Section 3.10 Lifecycle and Safety, Section 8 Safety and Reversibility, Section 3.7 Permission Manager.

- [ ] Unit + e2e green: TRIAL enable flow, kill switch, Reset Everything, ownership rollback; every safety transition logged with plugin ID + timestamp
- [ ] TRIAL timeout (30s per Section 8.1) defined ONCE as a named Core constant; UI beads (ymh.3, nir.4, jpr.1) reference it, never a second hardcoded value

Finder Sync extensions run in Finder process space. A blocking or crashing extension degrades Finder itself. The extension must be a minimal IPC client that hides (never blocks) when the daemon is down.

- [ ] Note: extension sends requests only, never executable code (Section 3.7 security model)

title: P0 Plugin API v1 contract (core/pkg/pluginapi): manifest, Decision enum, RegisterUI
description:
Parent: cross-os-ymh

## Background
P0 contract, must be reviewed before any plugin code (COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN.md Section 3.6, Section 3.6c, Phase 0 checklist). Locks the Plugin API v1 surface: plugins REGISTER behavior, Core owns the pipeline; no per-event fast-path callbacks.

## Reasoning
Go .so via plugin.Open() is explicitly REJECTED (OS/version/symbol fragility). MVP 0 ships builtin + declarative only; Level B executable is MVP 1. Locking this contract prevents plugin code from depending on unstable internals.

## Scope
- Manifest schema: ID, name, version, entry, type (builtin/declarative/executable/extpack), permissions, capabilities, config_schema, hooks, safety
- Lifecycle: DISABLED to TRIAL to ENABLED with rollback (Section 3.10)
- Decision enum (canonical, ONLY vocabulary): PASS / CONSUME / REPLACE with DecisionReplace normative note (suppress original + execute Intent; does NOT imply synthetic injection)
- apiVersion: independent manifestVersion / pluginApiVersion / capabilityApiVersion + minCoreVersion
- RegisterUI + UIContribution schema (Section 3.6c): namespaced IDs, declarative settings-page/section/sidebar MVP tier; custom-view REJECTED for MVP
- Hook semantics: onIntent/onEvent/onContext are async slow-path observers, never decision hooks
- Capability ownership: core IDs reserved, RegisterCapability rejects plugin shadowing

## Pass criteria
- [ ] pluginapi package (or proto/JSON schema) with Manifest, Registry, Decision, Capability, UIContribution, Hook types
- [ ] Ownership rule enforced in RegisterCapability (test: plugin claiming window.close fails)
- [ ] Contract reviewed + approved before any plugin code lands
- [ ] apiVersion fields present and checked at load

## Plan refs
COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN.md: Section 3.6 Plugin Runtime, Section 3.6c UI Contribution API, Section 3.10 Lifecycle, Section 3.12 registry.

title: P0 Intent + Capability contract (core/pkg/intent): schema-validated Intents, registry v1
description:
Parent: cross-os-ymh

## Background
P0 contract (COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN.md Section 3.4, Section 3.12, Glossary). Intent = platform-independent user goal (COPY, INTERRUPT, CLOSE_WINDOW); Action = concrete capability invocation; Capability = named privileged operation in the canonical registry. Core authority rule: Plugin requests, Core decides, Adapter executes.

## Reasoning
Without a locked intent vocabulary, plugins emit ad-hoc strings and adapters guess. The intent-first matrix (Section 6.1) then collapses into raw shortcut translation (e.g. wrong Alt+F4 to Cmd+Q instead of CLOSE_WINDOW).

## Scope
- Intent struct: versioned, schema-validated Parameters (never loose Action string + any-map)
- Capability API: request path plugin to Core to Adapter with permission checks
- Ownership split: core capabilities (canonical registry Section 3.12: input.*, window.*, clipboard.*, filesystem.*, app.*, finder.menu) implemented by Core/Adapter only; plugin-owned capabilities namespaced under plugin ID
- Canonical registry v1 with permission + platform + reversibility per capability

## Pass criteria
- [ ] Intent type + validation against target capability input schema
- [ ] Canonical registry v1 committed (all Section 3.12 IDs with version/permission/platforms/side-effects/reversible)
- [ ] Naming-convention lock documented: permission vs capability vs intent; invalid names (keyboard.intercept, window.manage) rejected
- [ ] Contract reviewed before plugin code

## Plan refs
COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN.md: Glossary, Section 3.4 Intent Resolver, Section 3.7 Permission Manager, Section 3.12 Capability Registry, Section 6.1 matrix.
- [ ] Registry validation unit-tested (unknown/invalid capability names rejected; Intent Parameters schema-validated); capability request path e2e with permission checks, traces logged

description:

## Background
COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN.md Section 3.11: Core taps every stage (event to context to rule to intent to action to result). Privacy model is normative: OFF / METADATA_ONLY (default) / DEBUG / FULL_TRACE. METADATA_ONLY redacts typed text, clipboard content, password fields. Replay tiers: Raw, Semantic, Capability (tier 2/3 are the primary debug loop).

Debugging shortcut failures by hand does not scale. Recorder + observe/dry-run mode (log Physical to Context to Rule to Intent to Would-execute WITHOUT executing) lets users validate new plugins before CrossOS modifies anything.

## Scope
- Recorder hook points at every pipeline stage
- Record: full trace per key event; Replay: deterministic re-run without live input
- Observe (dry-run) mode in Core (UI surfaces it in Phase 1)
- Privacy modes with METADATA_ONLY default + redaction; replay of semantic events only, never raw secrets

## Pass criteria
- [ ] Trace recorded per event across all six stages
- [ ] Replay reproduces a keyboard trace deterministically without live input
- [ ] METADATA_ONLY default verified: no typed text / clipboard content / password-field values in stored AND replayed traces (automated grep over fixture with synthetic secrets)
- [ ] Dry-run mode executes nothing while logging full Would-execute trace

COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN.md Section 3.3 + Data Flow step 2: FastContext rides the hot path with cache-resident fields only (AppID + AppMode, WindowID + class, DeviceID, modifiers). Per-keydown AX/UIA queries blow the under-1ms budget. Cache is updated on app/window/selection change; the keydown path only reads.

# Level B executable-plugin runtime (out-of-process JSON-RPC)



## Background

Phase 2 introduces PluginType `executable` (Level B, Â§3.6): plugins run as child processes speaking JSON-RPC over stdio/Unix socket from `~/.crossos/plugins/<id>/{manifest.json, plugin}`. Core spawns the executable; a plugin crash never takes down Core (restart/disable). MVP 0 shipped builtin + declarative only (Â§3.6 layout note: "Level B is MVP 1"). This runtime is also the gate for shell execution in extension packs (Phase 3: shell is opt-in Level B only, Â§6.3).



## Reasoning

- Go `.so` via `plugin.Open()` explicitly REJECTED (Â§3.6) â€” out-of-process is the only sanctioned native-code extension mechanism.

- Fast-path invariant (Â§2 Data Flow): external Level B plugins are compiled into the cached matcher ahead of time and NEVER run synchronously in the native callback â€” a 100ms plugin hang would break typing.

- Health states feed the Plugins UI page (Â§7.2: local-only in MVP 1+, no marketplace until Phase 4) and Phase 4 lifecycle (DISABLED/TRIAL/HEALTHY/ENABLED).

- Capability ownership (Â§3.6): RegisterCapability rejects plugin claims on core-owned IDs â€” enforce in the loader.



## Pass criteria

- [ ] Core spawns Level B executables, speaks JSON-RPC over stdio + Unix socket (framing reused from the 090 IPC contract, not a second protocol)

- [ ] Plugin crash â†’ Core survives â†’ restart/disable path exercised in test

- [ ] Health states reported (HEALTHY/ENABLED/DISABLED/TRIAL per Â§10 Phase 4 vocabulary, forward-compatible)

- [ ] Core-owned capability IDs rejected when a manifest tries to claim them

- [ ] Level B plugin rules compiled into cached fast matcher ahead of time; asserted no-synchronous-execution by test (decision callback never blocks on plugin IPC: marker/timeout probe fails the suite if the callback thread waits)



Plan refs: Â§3.6 (PluginType, layout, hooks), Â§2 Data Flow steps 3/7, Â§7.2 Plugins page, Â§10 Phase 2.

- [ ] Crash → restart/disable path covered by test with logged health-state transitions

# CI license/attribution merge gate (.github/workflows): Section 9.11 gate as a required job

## Background
Section 9.11 defines a load-bearing merge gate for any PR containing reused OSS code (pinned commit, license verified, transitive deps checked, copyright/NOTICE + ATTRIBUTION entry, merge) but no bead implements it as CI. Without automation the gate is advisory and GPL/no-license code can slip into the MIT core. Section 10 Phase 5 CI item and Section 11 merge-gate note both point here.

## Reasoning
- CrossOS is MIT: GPL/copyleft and no-license sources can never pass (Section 9.11). A required CI job that fails closed (missing pin/license/attribution means fail) is the only enforcement that survives scale.

- Builds on per-file attribution data (third_party repos LICENSE + NOTICE + ATTRIBUTION.md) from the reuse tasks.

- Required GitHub Actions job: detects reused-OSS files in the diff, asserts pinned commit + license-verified (not GPL/copyleft/no-license) + transitive-dep check + copyright/NOTICE + ATTRIBUTION.md entry present and well-formed
- Fail-closed on missing data; human-readable rejection citing the Section 9.11 gate step

## Pass criteria
- [ ] PR adding an MIT file with pinned commit + LICENSE + NOTICE + ATTRIBUTION.md entry passes (positive fixture)
- [ ] PR adding unattributed / GPL-licensed / no-license code fails with the correct gate-step message (fixture PRs)
- [ ] Job is required (blocks merge) on push + PR

Plan refs: Section 9.11 merge gate, Section 10 Phase 5 CI/CD, Section 12 CI/CD.

title: EventRouter behind EventBus interface (core/pkg/event): sync decision path, <1ms budget
description:
Parent: cross-os-ymh



## Background

COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN.md Section 3.2 + Data Flow: deterministic synchronous EventRouter behind an EventBus-named interface. Decision path is sync/bounded (inside the native callback); observation path is async/best-effort. Full pub/sub deferred until broadcast is genuinely needed.



## Reasoning

A generic goroutine/channel pub/sub on the hot path introduces ordering, backpressure, and subscription-lifecycle complexity before there are users â€” and risks the tap being disabled by timeout. The router keeps input to normalize to context to rule to action fully resolved before the callback returns.



## Scope

- Event/EventType/EventSource types (Section 3.2)

- EventBus interface (observation path) + EventRouter implementation (decision path)

- Fast path: callback returns PASS (original untouched) / CONSUME (block) / REPLACE (block + dispatch Intent); decided event enqueued as bounded async record AFTER return; slow path never feeds back into the same event

- Slow path: recorder, enrichment, UI log, plugin IPC observers



## Pass criteria

- [ ] Router resolves input to action synchronously with bounded latency (budget: intercept decision under 1ms)

- [ ] Slow-path work provably off the callback (no IPC, logging, or enrichment in decision path)

- [ ] Unit + e2e suites green: sync router resolution, conflict ranking, PASS/CONSUME/REPLACE semantics incl. Terminal INTERRUPT and CLOSE_WINDOW-not-quit

- [ ] Decision path binds the four P0 contracts: 2ha kill-switch check short-circuits the path, 4lm Decision enum is the only vocabulary, 9tb Intent/Capability is the action shape, xtk ranking picks the winner
- [ ] Every trace contains event → context → rule → intent → action → result stage logs (winner + losers); ae7 Recorder consumes these logs downstream (no reverse dependency: ae7 builds on z9v)

- [ ] Decision-path latency assertion (< 1ms) in suite or recorded benchmark



## Plan refs
